note: NAMING COLLISION: the census pins took the unprefixed noun, and eleven campaign readouts now carry the suffixed one.  IS the census pin file. Everything matching *_calibration.rs is a per-campaign preregistered readout, and there are eleven of them: burr, reticence, the_mire, the_fare, health, disposition, gathering, hearth_population, branches_family (all in windows/lab), approach_ease (worldgen), coercion (vessel). CONSEQUENCE FOR ANY OPERATOR GREP: a pattern like calibration\.rs matches all twelve, and anchoring it to windows/lab/ DOES NOT FIX IT -- eight of the eleven campaign readouts live in windows/lab too, so that anchor removes exactly one false positive and keeps eight. Measured by enumerating the tree, not reasoned. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE PREFIX, NOT THE DIRECTORY: /calibration\.rsmatches the census pins and nothing else; anything _calibration.rs is a campaign readout and needs ordinary review rather than census-pin review. WHY THIS IS A VOCABULARY PROBLEM AND NOT A GREP PROBLEM: two different concepts share one word -- a census pin is a frozen golden the calibration batteries assert against, a campaign readout is a preregistered measurement frozen before its own code. The incumbent took the bare noun, which is backwards; the specific instrument should have been namespaced and the general shape left free. Same shape The Coercion settled for possess vs dominate, and settled the same way: by counting. The readouts own the suffix eleven to one, so renaming them would be the expensive wrong direction. Recorded rather than fixed because a rename touches eleven files across three crates and the collision is cheap to live with once it is named.
